clue.text: Why issue a severe reprimand?

definitions.meaning: asking the reason for something, as in 'and that was for what purpose?'
to give someone a sharp telling-off is the idiom 'give them ___'

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what the point is of handing out a stern telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue a' sits between the two senses as a linking phrase: the idiom is 'give someone what for', a severe scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are idioms: the phrase asks for a purpose, and as a noun it means a sharp scolding.

clue.text: Yank runs into a young woman

indicators.note: the word runs goes into the young woman, so its letter is placed inside her

parts.note: wench is an old word for a young woman
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An American dashes towards a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American; here it is the verb meaning a sudden pull.
explanation.definitionFit: To yank and to wrench are both to pull or twist with a sudden violent jerk.

clue.text: Season fresh tuna without hesitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the rearranged fish surrounds the hesitation
fresh suggests a new version, so the letters of tuna are rearranged

parts.note: um is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A cook is told to season fresh tuna straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges the fish into AUTN, and 'without' (in its old sense of outside) wraps that round the hesitation. 'Season' looks like a cooking verb but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Autumn is one of the four seasons of the year, the one between summer and winter.

clue.text: Don't revoke injunction to conform

definitions.meaning: in card games to revoke is to fail to play a card of the suit led, so the instruction against it says play the same suit
to do as others have done

explanation.surface: An order that a court order must not be withdrawn, so that everyone complies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revoke' looks legal, beside 'injunction', but it is the card-game term for failing to play the suit led.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing a card of the same kind as the one led is the card rule; figuratively it means copying what others did.

clue.text: Butler to popular Israeli PM

parts.note: R. A. Butler, the British Conservative politician, was always known as Rab
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A servant serves a well-liked Israeli leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butler' looks like a servant; it is the British politician Rab Butler.
explanation.definitionFit: Yitzhak Rabin was twice prime minister of Israel, assassinated in 1995.

clue.text: Dutch city producing real ham

indicators.note: producing suggests the letters of the words are worked up into something new

explanation.surface: A city in the Netherlands known for making genuine ham.
explanation.definitionFit: Haarlem is a city in the Netherlands, capital of North Holland province.

clue.text: Swiss male, student vet and Scotsman

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
L is for learner, the plate on a learner driver's car
taken as written
Ian is the Scottish form of John, a stock Scottish name

explanation.surface: A list of people: a Swiss man, a veterinary student and a Scot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swiss' looks like an adjective on 'male'; it alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Helvetia is the Latin name for Switzerland, so the adjective formed from it means from that country.

clue.text: Coptic bishop in the spell of Swedish pop group

definitions.meaning: a title of honour given to bishops and patriarchs in the Coptic and other eastern churches, from the Aramaic for father
the 1970s band that won the Eurovision Song Contest with Waterloo

explanation.surface: An Egyptian churchman falls under the enchantment of a Scandinavian band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the spell of' only links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means father in Aramaic, used as a churchman's title, and is also the name of a famous Scandinavian band.

clue.text: Abandon Edward in a state of ferment

parts.note: to leave is to abandon
Ned is a pet name for Edward

explanation.surface: Leaving Edward behind causes turmoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ferment' suggests unrest, but here it is the literal rising of dough with yeast.
explanation.definitionFit: Dough that has been raised by yeast working through it is fermenting.

clue.text: Consider whether friend is about to publish

indicators.note: the friend is about, that is around, the other word, so it surrounds it

parts.note: mate is a friend
to edit is to prepare a text for publication

explanation.surface: Someone wonders if a pal is ready to bring out a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is about to' reads as 'is going to'; split it, so 'is about' makes the friend go round the word for preparing a text.
explanation.definitionFit: To meditate on something is to think it over deeply, to ponder.

clue.text: Praise given once to Labour leader

parts.note: ex means former, what something once was
taken as written

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tribute paid in the past to the head of the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour leader' looks like a party chief; it is just the first letter, L.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly, to laud.

clue.text: Invoice council for advertising space

parts.note: a bill is an invoice
a board is a governing council

explanation.surface: Sending a council a bill for putting up advertisements.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoarding on which posters are displayed is a large surface sold to advertisers.

clue.text: Naval officer got thrashed, but forbore to prosecute

parts.note: Com. is an abbreviation for commodore or commander, a naval rank
pounded means beaten hard

explanation.surface: A sailor was beaten up but declined to press charges.
explanation.walkthrough: In law, to compound a felony is to agree, usually for payment, not to prosecute it.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal sense: settling a crime privately for a consideration instead of bringing charges.

clue.text: Worst? Anything but!

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to worst someone is to defeat them

explanation.surface: Asked whether something was the poorest, the reply is that it was not at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worst' looks like the superlative of bad; first read it as the verb to defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat someone is both to worst and to outdo them, and the top quality is the opposite of the lowest.

clue.text: Puff perpetually whilst putting fetters on a donkey

parts.note: chains are fetters
moke is British slang for a donkey

explanation.surface: Someone keeps smoking while shackling an ass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whilst putting ... on a' just links the pieces; MOKE is an informal British word for a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: To light one cigarette from the last, drawing on them continuously.

clue.text: This man's tone caused great surprise

indicators.note: caused signals that the words are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A man's tone of voice shocked everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'man's' is ignored; THIS MAN'S TONE has the twelve letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazement is a feeling of great surprise or wonder.

clue.text: Grandiose design methodically developed

indicators.note: to design is to arrange, so the letters of the word are laid out afresh

explanation.surface: A grand plan worked out step by step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' looks like the anagram signal, but 'design' rearranges GRANDIOSE and 'methodically developed' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arranged in a systematic, orderly way has been methodically put together.

clue.text: Make lively lad embrace spellbinding lady

indicators.note: the lad embraces the lady, holding her inside

parts.note: a son is a lad
a witch is a woman who casts spells

explanation.surface: A boy hugs an enchanting woman and comes alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spellbinding' sounds like praise; here it literally means casting spells.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn on is, figuratively, to become animated or to excite.

clue.text: Damned healthy!

definitions.meaning: a mild British swear word, used like bloody

explanation.surface: An exclamation that someone is in rude good health.
explanation.walkthrough: The British mild oath means 'damned'; the other sense is of a person or plant flourishing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a polite British swear word, and also means flourishing like a plant in flower.

clue.text: Stepping on the gas in elated mood

parts.note: walking is stepping
taken as written
air is a mixture of gases

explanation.surface: A driver puts a foot down on the accelerator while feeling cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stepping on the gas' is American for accelerating; read literally, it is treading on air.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone so joyful they seem to float, thrilled.

clue.text: Bill is allowed to take a pill

parts.note: tab is a bill, as in picking up the tab
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Bill is permitted some medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name; it is the bill to pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablet is a small pressed dose of medicine.

clue.text: Provide plaster

definitions.meaning: to give or supply a service
to coat a wall with a layer of plaster or cement

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to give, and builders also use it for coating a wall in a first layer.

clue.text: Hardy sergeant in the city of Paris

definitions.meaning: the dashing sergeant in Thomas Hardy's novel Far from the Madding Crowd
Paris was the prince of the ancient city besieged by the Greeks

explanation.surface: A tough soldier serves in the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' looks like an adjective, 'tough'; it is the novelist. 'Paris' is the Trojan prince, not the French capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergeant Frank Troy is the soldier in Hardy's novel, and Paris's home city was the one in the Iliad.

clue.text: Very poorly and with little muscular tone

explanation.surface: Someone is quite unwell and out of condition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both ill and physically unfit, lacking condition.

clue.text: A marine detachment in church

parts.note: an isle is a piece of land detached from the mainland in the sea

explanation.surface: A unit of Royal Marines is stationed in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marine detachment' suggests a troop of soldiers; it is land cut off by the sea. The definition says where the answer is found.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage between pews is found inside a church building.

clue.text: Criminal providing grass

definitions.meaning: British slang for corrupt or crooked
a type of stiff, wiry grass

explanation.surface: A crook is acting as an informer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' looks like British slang for an informer; it is the plant species.
explanation.definitionFit: Crooked and dishonest, in British slang; also the name of a common pasture plant.

clue.text: Women expected to succeed

parts.note: reads as ambitious women tipped for success, but means women who will inherit an estate or title

explanation.definitionFit: Women next in line to inherit a fortune will succeed to it, taking it over when the holder dies.

clue.text: Restored lodge eyed with longing

indicators.note: restored means rebuilt, so the letters of the building are put back together differently

explanation.surface: A renovated country house was admired with envy.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to stare at with desire.

clue.text: Denied necessity to carry a revolver

indicators.note: the necessity carries the revolver, holding it inside

parts.note: need is a necessity
gat is old slang for a gun

explanation.surface: Someone denies they needed to carry a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate is to deny or nullify a claim.

clue.text: German prince becomes English university teacher

parts.note: a lector is a university lecturer, especially abroad

explanation.surface: A German royal takes up a post teaching at an English university.
explanation.walkthrough: The princes who chose the Holy Roman Emperor were called Electors.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Holy Roman Empire certain princes held the right to vote for the emperor.
